questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: A rigid motion carries △ABC onto △DEF with A → D, B → E, C → F. Explain why AB = DE, BC = EF, CA = FD, ∠A ≅ ∠D, ∠B ≅ ∠E, and ∠C ≅ ∠F.
questions.prompt_markup: A rigid motion carries △ABC onto △DEF with A → D, B → E, C → F. Explain why AB = DE, BC = EF, CA = FD, ∠A ≅ ∠D, ∠B ≅ ∠E, and ∠C ≅ ∠F.
questions.correct_answer: Each side and angle of ABC is carried onto the corresponding side and angle of DEF, and rigid motions keep lengths and angle measures.
questions.required_method: Use the definition: the motion sends each vertex to its partner, so it sends each side and angle onto the corresponding one, and rigid motions keep length and angle measure.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: (1) the motion maps segment AB onto segment DE (endpoints to endpoints), and similarly for the other sides and angles; (2) rigid motions preserve distance and angle measure. Invalid: "they look the same".

questions.prompt: In △ABC and △DEF, AB = DE, BC = EF, CA = FD, ∠A ≅ ∠D, ∠B ≅ ∠E, and ∠C ≅ ∠F. Explain how to build a rigid motion that carries △ABC onto △DEF.
questions.prompt_markup: In △ABC and △DEF, AB = DE, BC = EF, CA = FD, ∠A ≅ ∠D, ∠B ≅ ∠E, and ∠C ≅ ∠F. Explain how to build a rigid motion that carries △ABC onto △DEF.
questions.correct_answer: A translation, a rotation, and (if needed) a reflection carry A to D, B to E, and C to F.
questions.required_method: Translate A to D; rotate about D so ray AB lies on ray DE (B lands on E because AB = DE); if C is on the other side of line DE from F, reflect across DE. Explain why C then lands on F.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: the translation and rotation match A and B; the reflection (if needed) puts C on F's side; C lands on F because ∠A ≅ ∠D puts C on ray DF and AC = DF fixes its distance from D. Accept using ∠B and ∠E instead. Invalid: stating the result without explaining why C lands on F.
